questions.def: 'Had' requires a past participle to form the past perfect conditional.
questions.question: Had he ___ the instructions carefully, the experiment would have succeeded.

questions.def: 'Such' requires inversion of the verb in formal contexts.
questions.question: Such ___ her dedication, she quickly rose through the ranks.

questions.def: 'Arguable' fits as an adjective modifying 'points'.
questions.question: The ___ points were presented with clarity and precision.

questions.def: 'Were it to' is a formal conditional construction.
questions.question: Were it ___ to rain, the match would be postponed.

questions.def: 'Little' requires inversion with 'did' for emphasis.
questions.question: Little ___ she know, her efforts would soon be rewarded.

questions.def: 'Unintended' correctly describes the unexpected consequences.
questions.question: The ___ consequences of the policy were far-reaching.

questions.def: 'So' at the start requires verb inversion: 'was she'.
questions.question: So dedicated ___ she that she worked through the night.

questions.def: 'No sooner... than' is the correct correlative conjunction.
questions.question: No sooner had he arrived ___ the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Perceptive' acts as an adjective meaning insightful.
questions.question: His ___ understanding of the situation was remarkable.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires inversion using 'did'.
questions.question: Only then ___ I realise the enormity of the problem.

questions.def: 'Were there' is a formal conditional construction.
questions.question: Were ___ any objections, we shall proceed.

questions.def: 'Unknowing' means lacking knowledge and starts an absolute phrase.
questions.question: ___ of his whereabouts, the police launched a search.

questions.def: 'Not a word' is the idiomatic expression.
questions.question: Not a ___ did she utter during the entire ordeal.

questions.def: 'Under no circumstances' requires inversion: 'will this'.
questions.question: Under no circumstances ___ be tolerated.

questions.def: 'Regardless' correctly conveys the lack of consideration of rain.
questions.question: ___ of rain, the event proceeded as planned.

questions.def: 'At no time' requires inversion with 'did'.
questions.question: At no time ___ I suspect his true motives.

questions.def: 'Only by' requires inversion: 'can you'.
questions.question: Only by working hard ___ achieve success.

questions.def: Inverted conditional: 'Had she imagined' = 'If she had imagined'.
questions.question: ___ the consequences, she would never have acted.

questions.def: 'Were he here' is a formal conditional construction.
questions.question: Were he ___, I would have helped him.

questions.def: 'Not until' requires inversion with 'did'.
questions.question: Not until I saw it ___ I believe it.

questions.def: 'Denying' starts a participial phrase modifying 'he'.
questions.question: ___ the allegations, he maintained his innocence.

questions.def: 'Much to his surprise' is the correct idiom.
questions.question: Much ___ his surprise, he won the lottery.

questions.def: 'Had I known' is the correct inverted conditional form.
questions.question: Had ___ known, I would have acted differently.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'Had I known' implies 'If I had known'.
questions.question: Had I known, I ___ you.

questions.def: 'Owing to' introduces a cause in a formal context.
questions.question: ___ the rain, the match was postponed.

questions.def: Passive voice after 'It was': 'It was suggested'.
questions.question: It was ___ that he resign.

questions.def: Inversion after 'So': 'So + adjective + was + he'.
questions.question: So ___ was he that he forgot his keys.

questions.def: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund or 'having' + past participle.
questions.question: He denied ___ the money.

questions.def: Perfect participle clause: 'Having been informed' implies prior action.
questions.question: ___ of the changes, he acted accordingly.

questions.def: Inverted conditional: 'Had he persevered' = 'If he had persevered'.
questions.question: ___, he would have succeeded.
